steps.title: Welcome to Dossiq
steps.body: Dossiq handles cases from intake to archive. Load the demo data to see it work. Then initialise the register and schemas.

steps.title: Load example data?
steps.body: Example data fills the lists, detail pages and dashboards so you can see the app working straight away. Pick "None" on a production install.

steps.title: Load the example data
steps.body: Loads what you picked. The data is obviously sample data, it is safe to run more than once, and you can delete it afterwards.

dwangsom_callback_secret.title: Callback signing secret
dwangsom_callback_secret.description: Shared secret the payment provider signs its dwangsom payout callbacks with. Until it is set, DwangsomPaymentCallbackController cannot verify that a callback really came from the provider. Only shown while the dwangsom payout integration is configured.

steps.title: Welcome to Dossiq
steps.body: Let's take a quick spin through case handling. We'll register a case together so you can see how the pieces fit, and you'll add the record yourself.
Cases are the heart of your work. Open Cases from the menu to see everything in progress.
Register your first case. Give it a title, pick a case type, then save. You can add tasks, decisions and documents later.
steps.task: Click New and save a case

steps.title: Where case types come from
steps.body: Every case follows a case type, its blueprint. The case type decides the statuses a case moves through, how long it may take, who handles it and what may be decided. Have a look; you do not need to make one, 88 ship with the app.
steps.task: Open Case types in the menu

steps.title: Where the automation lives
steps.body: Flows are what happens without anyone clicking: a deadline that warns before it passes, a confirmation that goes out on submission. This is where you read and edit them. Nothing to build now.
Your work lives here. Open My Work to see the tasks and cases assigned to you.
steps.task: Click My Work in the menu

steps.title: Your first case is on the board
steps.body: The Dashboard tracks progress as cases move through it. The documentation covers the rest.
steps.task: Open the documentation to keep going

config.description: Cases, deadlines and your workload at a glance

widgets.title: Open Cases
widgets._note: openspec/specs/dashboard/spec.md DASH-001a: this card counts every case whose status is not final, and is deliberately NOT scoped to the dashboard date range. It used to be titled "New cases" and counted startDate inside the picker window, which answers a different question and left the dashboard with no headline for open workload at all. The spec's "+3 today" sub-label is not expressible here: CnStatWidget interpolates a caption only in endpointSource mode, so a second count needs a Dossiq KPI endpoint.

widgets.title: SLA Compliance
widgets._note: openspec/specs/dashboard/spec.md DASH-001e. Reads the share of this month's closed cases whose endDate met their deadline, computed server-side by KpiAggregationService. Clicking opens the doorlooptijd dashboard, as the scenario requires.

widgets.title: My work
widgets._note: openspec/changes/dashboard-tiles design D1. Replaces `my-tasks` and `task-reminders`, which read the same schema with the same filter and differed only in a due-date window, so seven of ten rows appeared on the page twice. `extend` carries `case` as well as `calculations`: a $ref column renders the stored uuid unless the referenced object is extended AND the column reads `<property>.<labelField>`, which is why the case column is keyed `case.title`. `rowActions` Pick up and Complete stay blocked on nextcloud-vue (the 2.40.0 object-table vocabulary has no such key); the row keeps `rowRoute` to TaskDetail, where the lifecycle buttons already render.

widgets.title: Deadlines
widgets._note: openspec/changes/dashboard-tiles design D1. Replaces `overdue-cases` and `deadline-alerts`, which read `case` with the same `isFinalStatus: false` filter and differed only in the deadline window, so seven of nine rows appeared twice. One window now covers both: everything already past its deadline and everything due within three days, ordered by deadline. The red row is `rowClass`, not the `cn-cell--danger` the design sketched: a column's `cellClass` is one static string, so it cannot carry a per-branch colour, and the spec asks for the ROW to read in the error colour anyway.

content._viewAllNote: one-case-list A22, triage item 4. The query is this table's OWN filter in the flat bracket grammar, key for key, and `dashboardViewAllRoutes.spec.js` holds that invariant for every tile: a table that counts one set of cases and a View all that lands on another is the dropped filter this fixes. The nested `{ deadline: { lte } }` form belongs in a `source.filter`, which the widget reads, and NOT in a route query, which `buildQueryString` would JSON-stringify into a literal object string that matches nothing. Note the WINDOW: this table is overdue AND due within three days, wider than the Cases page's Overdue chip, so it deliberately does not carry that chip's filter. `kpi-overdue` is the widget whose count the Overdue chip reproduces exactly, and that equality is asserted. CnIndexPage merges the query into the fetch under the page's own filter, so the filter arrives and the list is right; what it does NOT do is activate a matching chip, because `resolveInitialQuickFilterIndex` reads only `default`. The reader lands on All with the query applied and no chip showing why, and naming a chip from a query needs a nextcloud-vue change.
content.emptyText: No deadlines in the next three days

pages.title: Queue
pages._note: The one queue: every case that is open and that nobody has picked up. It is a FILTER over `case`, not a collection of its own, so this is a plain type:index rather than a bespoke view. `assignee: "IS NULL"` is the literal sentinel every OpenRegister condition builder matches by value. The suffix spelling `assignee_isnull=true` was dead when this page shipped: the only code that mentioned it had no callers, and `isnull` was missing from MagicSearchHandler::COMPARISON_OPERATORS, so the filter contributed no condition at all. Fixed in openregister `isnull-filter-operator`; the sentinel is kept because it also works on instances that do not yet carry that change. `isFinalStatus: false` keeps closed cases out; it is a real boolean on every case row, not a derived one, so plain equality reaches it. Assigning a case removes it from here and puts it on that person's Assigned to me; All cases shows it either way. The caseType folder sidebar is the same control the Cases index uses, so the queue narrows by case type without a second page. WHY THIS IS A PAGE AND NOT A `menu[].query` PRESET, which is what gate-68 (ADR-097 Decision 5) proposes for a second index over an already-indexed schema: a preset is only a link into the target page, where the query filters and the reader's own facet filters share one map, so a facet interaction can widen the queue back to every case. A base filter on the page itself cannot be cleared by the person reading it, and that is the property that makes the queue trustworthy. Assigned to me is a page for the same reason.

config.emptyText: Nothing is waiting. Every open case has someone on it.

pages.title: My Work
pages._note: Case index scoped to the current user (assignee = current uid) in card view. A thin CnIndexPage wrapper because the stock index base-filter does not resolve the @me current-user token; the wrapper injects the resolved uid.

pages.title: Cases
pages._note: `excludeFields: [status]` keeps the status picker OFF this page's form dialog, and the reason is not cosmetic. On CREATE the picker listed every case type's statuses. CnFormDialog loads a reference field's options once, at open time, and `status` carries `x-relation-filter: { caseType: "@object.caseType" }`: a token that resolves to nothing while the form is still empty, so the fetch goes out unfiltered and never goes out again. Half those options are named `Received` or `In progress`, belong to a different case type, and are therefore both indistinguishable and wrong. A case is born with its own case type's `initialStatus` through `x-openregister-prefill`, so there is no status a person should be picking here at all. On EDIT the token does resolve and the picker is correctly scoped, but a raw dropdown writes the field straight through: no statusRecord, no guard evaluation, none of the transition's `automaticActions`. A status is the OUTPUT of a transition, not a field. CaseDetail's `lifecycleActions.field: status` is where one changes.

config._bulkActionsNote: one-case-list A21. Bulk work stopped at Reassign while `BulkTransitionDialog` and `BulkStatusTransitionService` already served the workflow board, so the four gestures a handler does most from a list were reachable only one case at a time. Each handler opens the SAME dialog in its own mode with a required reason: Suspend, Resume and Extend term are statutory acts (Awb 4:5 and 4:14) someone has to justify later, and doing twenty at once is exactly when the justification goes unwritten. The handlers are FUNCTIONS in src/customComponents.js, not the declarative `handler: "open-modal"` path: that path emits an `open-modal` event nothing in the library listens for, so declaring it would ship a bulk action that does nothing when clicked. Every icon here is registered in src/icons.js (hydra gate-60); a name that is not renders no icon at all rather than a fallback glyph.
config._teamColumnNote: `assignedGroup` is a $ref to an organisatieRol and CnIndexPage renders a plain key raw, so the column would show a uuid. `extend` asks OpenRegister to expand the reference on the fetch and the column reads the expanded row's `roleName`, the same shape the Tasks index uses for `case.title`; the server cannot sort on a nested field, so the column is not sortable. The Team FACET in the sidebar comes from `facetable: true` on the property itself and is the interim for the blocked Team chip.
config._quickFiltersNote: one-case-list, D1 revised: the Queue page and the My Work page stay exactly as they are, and no menu entry changes. These chips only add the lenses to the list that already exists. Unclaimed carries the SAME two conditions as Queue's base filter (`assignee: "IS NULL"`, `isFinalStatus: false`), literally equal so the two lists cannot drift; the manifest vitest asserts that equality rather than trusting it. ALL IS THE DEFAULT, not Mine: `resolveInitialQuickFilterIndex` activates the chip marked `default` (and the FIRST chip when none is), so a Mine default would silently narrow every reader's first paint to their own cases and make an empty list look like an empty register. Ruben's revision to the change's own 'Mine is the default' decision; the same pattern parties-on-the-case established. Overdue spells its operator as the flat `deadline[lt]` key, not the nested `{ deadline: { lt } }` object: `buildQueryString` JSON-stringifies a nested object value, which reaches the API as the literal string `{"lt":"@today"}` and matches nothing. `@today` resolves client-side to `YYYY-MM-DD` at fetch time.

columns.label: Status
columns._note: The Status column reads the status's own colour. `statusTypeName` alone resolves the $ref to a name and stops there, so five different statuses read as one grey column. A cell WIDGET rather than a second formatter, for the reason cellWidgets.js gives: a formatter returns a string and a string cannot carry a colour. The formatter stays as the fallback label the widget renders while the statusType collection is still loading.

columns.label: Deadline
columns._note: one-case-list A22. A raw ISO date makes every reader do the same subtraction once per row and get it wrong on the rows that matter. `deadlineCountdown` (src/services/cellWidgets.js) renders the days left and, past the deadline, the days overdue in the signalering red. A cell WIDGET rather than a `formatter` because a formatter returns a string and a string cannot carry the overdue state; nextcloud-vue 2.41 ships no built-in countdown cell, only `CnCountdownWidget` for a dashboard tile. The column stays sortable: CnDataTable sorts on the stored `deadline`, not on the rendered text.

config._note: CASE archetype (unified zaak) — the flagship record and the ADR-062 reference page (the cell is the budget: every widget fills its gridHeight exactly, no inner scrollbars, no reserved voids). The lead row pairs the field-scoped 'Core case data' widget (include: identity/ownership fields) with a right column of KPI stats-block (open tasks / documents / decisions / sub-cases, replacing the deprecated header summaryAggregates) over the Related panel. Row two pairs the 'Process' data widget (include: status/procedure/workflow fields) with Initiator, Contacts and Notes sized to their small content. FK-scoped child collections (task.case, caseDocument.case, decision.case, location.case) fit their rows to their cells with View-all/+N-more footers. Files and Calendar leaves close the page. The case's own state leads the page: a full-width transition strip (case-transitions) over the KPI row, whose third cell is now the stepper (case-steps) rather than the milestone percentage. `lifecycleActions` is GONE -- it declared `{field: status}` and rendered nothing, because OpenRegister answers no actions for a $ref status field. Suspend, Resume, Extend term and Reopen are `open-modal` header actions onto one reason dialog (CaseLifecycleActionDialog), which reads /lifecycle before it posts. Only Reopen gates exactly as the spec words it, because `isFinalStatus` is on the case record: an action's local `visibleWhen` dot-paths into the loaded record, `suspensionAllowed` and `extensionAllowed` live on the case TYPE, and OpenRegister's object list IGNORES an `id` filter (it answers with the whole table), so a `source` predicate on the type would compare a different case type's flag and be wrong without saying so. Suspension is derived from the case's `activity` journal rather than a flag, so no field can gate Resume either -- the transitions widget puts Resume in front of the handler when /lifecycle says the case is actually suspended. Audit history stays the single sidebar tab.

widgets.title: Core case data
widgets._note: `identifier` carries `readOnly: true` in the schema because OpenRegister generates it, and fieldsFromSchema DROPS a readOnly property outright unless an override re-admits it. So the case number sat in this include list and rendered nowhere at all — the very field five of the seven demo cases were reported as missing. The `identifier` override re-admits the field with `readOnly: false` and then keeps it un-editable with `editable: false`, which is the state the requirement asks for: shown, never typed.

widgets.title: Terms and archive
widgets._note: The statutory block: what the law gives you for this case, and what happens to the file afterwards. Every field here already existed on the schema and every one of them carried `visible: false`, which drops a property from every schema-driven surface at once, so the fields were declared and unreadable rather than merely unplaced. `statutoryTerm` is the type's processing deadline copied onto the case: the design asked for `extend` plus the include path `caseType.processingDeadline`, but a data widget builds its fields from the schema's OWN properties, so a dotted include matches nothing and renders nothing, and the stat-caption fallback interpolates only an endpoint payload. `hideEmpty` stays off on purpose: a case with no archive action date must show the row empty, because an absent destruction date is itself the thing a records officer is looking for.

widgets.title: Hours booked
widgets._note: The Log hours header action books time against THIS case; its `props` are seed values rather than fields a person fills in, because humaniq keeps domainObjectRef and domainObjectType out of every includeFields allowlist on purpose (they are written by integrations, not typed by an employee). Hours live in humaniq, per ADR-107 decision 6: 'Hours logged on a case are hrmq time entries carrying the case reference.' This tile used to sum shillinq UrenRegistratie on subjectApp/subjectId, which contradicted that ADR and, worse, could only ever read zero: a fleet-wide grep found NO writer for subjectApp anywhere, so the tile reported 0 hours on every case in every install and looked correct doing it. The retirement of the shillinq path is tracked in shillinq openspec/changes/hours-to-humaniq. `dossiq:case` is the `<app>:<schema>` literal humaniq documents; it is the app <id> in appinfo/info.xml, and dossiq is the first writer of it in the fleet.

widgets.title: Initiator
widgets._note: Initiator (indiener) display — brp-kvk register sets. Resolved via page slots (widget-initiator -> InitiatorSection); self-fetches the case from the route id and renders nothing when no initiator is set.

widgets.title: Sub-cases
widgets._note: deelzaak-support REQ 'Sub-cases section on parent case detail': 'The case detail view SHALL display a "Sub-cases" section ... listing all cases whose parentCase references the current case. The section MUST show each sub-case's title, status, assignee, and deadline.' Only the stats-block COUNT (case-kpis-sub-cases) existed; the listing lived on a separate route (/cases/:id/deelzaken, DeelzaakList), so the detail view had no such section and the requirement was unimplemented. The count widget already proves the filter shape works. Rows deep-link to CaseDetail because a sub-case IS a case.

widgets.title: Tasks
widgets._note: task-on-the-case A06: the Tasks tab shows the first OPEN task of this case with the lifecycle buttons OpenRegister answers for it, confirms a completion with a toast and puts the next open task in its place, so a handler finishes a task without leaving the case. The id, the title, the icon, the tab entry and every content key are unchanged, and no page is added or retyped, so the ADR-100 page ratchet does not move. TYPE is the interim. [blocked: nextcloud-vue 2.41.1 CnObjectListWidget has no rowActions and no lifecycle column] so a button cannot be put inside a row from configuration; verified against the installed 2.40.0 dist and the published 2.41.1 tarball. TARGET: back to type object-list with a lifecycle column (asked for in https://github.com/ConductionNL/nextcloud-vue/issues/1033), at which point src/components/tasks/CaseTaskPane.vue and its registry entry are deleted. The type names the registry key rather than "custom" because this widget is a child of the case-panels tabs widget: CnDetailPage renders a widget-<id> page slot per GRID item only, and CnTabsWidget resolves a tab child through cnRegistry[widget.type], rendering nothing at all when no key answers. content.columns, content.rowRoute and content.emptyText are kept as written: they are what the widget goes back to reading the day the library grows the column.

content.emptyText: No tasks for this case yet

widgets.title: Parties
widgets._note: parties-on-the-case D1: everyone involved in THIS case, read straight off the `role` schema. `RolesTab.vue` is an admin surface over every role row in the register, so it can never answer the case page's question; this widget is the same object-list shape `case-tasks` and `case-sub-cases` already use, filtered on `case: @objectId`. `roleType` is a $ref and CnIndexPage renders a $ref column raw, so that cell shows a uuid until nextcloud-vue renders label fields for reference columns (triage #8, Tier D06); `participant` carries the readable identity in the meantime. `delegate` and `delegateUntil` are shown as the plain window they are — whether a delegate is active NOW is the substitution resolver's answer, not this list's. Absent from `layout` like every other tab child: the tabs widget renders it, so a layout entry would render it twice.

content.emptyText: No parties on this case yet
No locations linked to this case yet

widgets.title: Flow runs
widgets._note: case-flow-human-steps 6.1, the case half: this case's own flow run and the step it sits on, with its finished runs underneath (nextcloud-vue CnFlowRunsWidget in subject mode). `subject: '@objectId'` binds the current case, so OpenRegister filters the active and completed reads to it server-side. `rowRoute` and not `runRoute` on purpose: dossiq has no run detail page, and FlowDetail (/flows/:id) resolves a FLOW id, so a click opens the flow whose sidebar lists its runs. Pointing runRoute at FlowDetail would push a run uuid into a flow route and open nothing.

content.subject: @objectId
content.emptyText: No flow is running for this case

widgets.title: Case status
widgets._note: The transitions this user may take from the case's current status, the confirm dialog that asks for a comment and, on a closing move, a result, plus the suspended marker and the Resume button (page slot widget-case-transitions -> CaseTransitionsWidget). It replaces the page's `lifecycleActions: {field: status}` block, which rendered NOTHING: CnLifecycleActions asks OpenRegister's /available-actions, and `case.status` is a $ref to a per-caseType statusType row, for which OR answers an empty action list. Its graph mode derives moves from sibling ORDER alone and so cannot express the workflow template's named, role-filtered, guarded transitions, cannot say which guard refused, and cannot ask for the result a closing case needs -- all three of which this page requires. When the platform can serve them (case-status-onto-engine-lifecycle), this widget is deleted and lifecycleActions declared again.

widgets.title: Time left
widgets._note: Counts down to the case deadline. Reads `deadline` off the record the page has already loaded, so it costs no request. The thresholds follow the handling rhythm rather than round numbers: at two weeks a handler still has room to act, at five days they do not. An overdue case reads as an alert whether or not thresholds are set.

widgets.title: Case type
widgets._note: `case.caseType` holds a uuid, which is not something to show a person, so `resolve` looks the case type's title up through the shared object store (cached per schema, deduplicated in flight). An id that cannot be resolved keeps showing the raw value rather than blanking: a blank KPI says nothing at all.

widgets.title: Steps
widgets._note: Which step the case is in, over its case type's statusType rows in `order` (page slot widget-case-steps -> CaseStepsWidget). It takes the cell the milestone progress tile had, and that tile is gone: milestones are configured on almost no case type, so `Completed` read 0% on every demo case and told a handler nothing, while every case has a status because a case cannot exist without one. The milestone endpoint stays for its other readers; this page simply stops calling it. A `stepper` widget type over a reference field's ordered sibling rows would make this a config declaration (tasks 3.3); until nextcloud-vue ships one, the custom widget is the interim. Many statuses in a four-column cell scroll sideways rather than clipping, which is the honest failure mode for a case type with a long process.

widgets.title: Mail & messages
widgets._note: The mail leaf as a body widget so it can be a tab. The sidebar CaseEmailTab stays: the sidebar is for reading alongside the case, the tab is for working in it.

widgets.title: Communication
widgets._note: Every call, visit and message logged on this case, newest first. The contactmoment schema was the KCC workplace's alone and no case page read it; `contactmoment.case` is the single case reference the object-list filter needs, because `relatedCases` is a list and a list cannot be a filter. Notes and Mail stay their own tabs until a tabs entry can render several widgets as stacked sections (design D4). The Log contact header action beside this list seeds FOUR values through `props`, not just the case: design D3 has ContactMomentService fill the KCC fields the form does not ask for, which holds for the API path (ContactMomentController) but not for this one, because an open-form action saves straight to /apps/openregister/api/objects and no dossiq service runs. `contactmoment` requires identificationMethod, kccEmployeeId and nature, so without the seeds every save from that button answers 400 with the required list. Seeded values are written and never rendered: CnFormDialog takes its fields from includeFields and merges initialData over the form data, so the handler still sees the five fields the spec names. `relatedCases` is seeded from the same token because the KCC voorblad reads that list; ContactMomentService does the same for the API path, where the service DOES run.

content.emptyText: No contact logged on this case yet

widgets.title: Documents
widgets._note: The case file, on the case page. `zaakinformatieobject` rows for this case, rendered through DossierTab: title, type, status, direction, date and author, the drop zone that writes an informatieobject plus its join, and the version panel per row. Five of the six columns live on the REFERENCED informatieobject and CnObjectListWidget renders a `$ref` column as the raw reference, so the interim is a custom widget type rather than an `object-list` over `zaakinformatieobject` (change documents-on-the-case, task 2.2). The type is `dossier-tab` and NOT `custom`: a `type: "custom"` widget resolves through the page's `widget-<id>` slot, which CnDetailPage renders only for LAYOUT grid items, so inside a tab panel it renders nothing and says nothing — CnTabsWidget dispatches its children through CnDetailWidgetHost, which resolves a renderer by widget TYPE against the consumer registry (REQ-MVR-005). Deliberately absent from `layout`: the tabs widget renders it, and a layout entry would render it twice. The Files tab stays beside it for loose attachments and Nextcloud shares.

widgets.title: Case panels
widgets._note: Six panels describing one case used to be six cards stacked down the page, each with its own header and Actions menu, only one of them ever being read. The strip takes over the title and the card, the children render bare, and the Actions menu is hoisted into the bar where it rebinds to whichever tab is open. The six children stay in `widgets` and are DELIBERATELY absent from `layout`: the tabs widget renders them, so a layout entry would render each one twice.

tabs.label: Tags
tabs._note: A sidebar tab renders EITHER a registered `component` or `widgets[]` whose `type` is a CnObjectSidebar built-in (data, metadata, audit / audit-trail, object-table). A `type: "custom"` entry here resolves to nothing and renders an empty panel with a console warning nobody reads — the page-slot mechanism (`widget-<id>`) only applies to layout grid items. So this is the `data` built-in over the single `tags` field: it is handed the loaded case and the resolved schema by the host, and an array-of-strings property already resolves to the tags editor. The `widget` override says so out loud, so a later change to the type cannot silently turn the editor into a text box.

pages.title: Sub-cases
pages._note: Bespoke parent-scoped sub-case (deelzaak) list: header carries a back-to-parent button, a parent breadcrumb link and a roll-up summary line, and rows deep-link into DeelzaakDetail under the same parent route. A standard list/index type can't express the parent-route binding (/cases/:id/deelzaken) plus the parent-context header and roll-up text.

pages.title: Sub-case
pages._note: Sub-case detail that shares the `case` schema with CaseDetail but adds a mandatory always-visible parent breadcrumb (parent → current) and a link out to the canonical CaseDetail edit view. The standard detail type renders a single object with no parent-context breadcrumb or cross-route hand-off, so the parent-aware framing requires a bespoke page.

config._note: OBJECTION-CASE archetype (AWB bezwaar), ADR-062 round 2. `bezwaar` is a supporting schema on a unified case (bezwaar.case) and declares NO comms linkedTypes — so NO files/notes/contacts/calendar leaves here; those live on the parent CaseDetail. The lead row pairs the field-scoped 'Objection' core widget (case/objection/status/awbReference/ontvangstdatum/decisionDeadline) with an in-grid KPI stats-block (advice-request and decision counts, replacing the deprecated header summaryAggregates). The AWB statutory-clock fields (verdaging/opschorting/hearing waiver/ingebrekestelling/dwangsom) are a genuinely distinct group and get their own 'Statutory clock & suspension' data widget. The two real child collections follow as FK-scoped object-lists side by side: committee advice requests (bacAdviceRequest.bezwaar) and decisions on the objection (bezwaarDecision.bezwaar), each deep-linking to its own detail page. lifecycleActions drive the bezwaar status (Ontvangen → … → Afgehandeld). Audit history stays a sidebar tab.

content.emptyText: No advice requests raised for this objection yet
No decisions recorded for this objection yet

config._note: DECISION-RECORD archetype (beslissing op bezwaar, AWB art. 7:11), ADR-062 round 2. No comms linkedTypes and no child schemas point at it. The 17-field schema splits into two genuinely distinct groups: 'Disposition & reasoning' (the legal substance — dispositionType, reasoning, legalBasis, advisoryOpinion, followsAdvice, deviationRationale, proceskostenvergoeding, status) paired with the Related panel (parent bezwaar and case), and 'Publication & documents' (the formal paper trail — replacementDecision, appealNotice, dates, decisionMaker, decisionDocument, publishedAt, notifiedRecipients) full-width below. lifecycleActions drive the status (draft → published). No files/notes leaves: document references are plain fields, not a files-leaf. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config._columnsNote: `case` is a $ref to the case and CnIndexPage renders a plain key raw, so the column showed truncated uuids. `extend` asks OpenRegister to expand the reference on the fetch and the column reads the expanded object's title; the server cannot sort on a nested field, so the column is not sortable.
config._quickFiltersNote: one-case-list: the same three lenses the Cases index carries, in the same order and with the same labels, so a person who learned one list has learned the other. `isTerminalStatus` is the task-side twin of the case's `isFinalStatus` and is a stored boolean, so plain equality reaches it. All stays the default chip for the reason spelled out on Cases.

config._note: ACTION-ITEM archetype — a work item on a case (task.case) with assignee/dueDate/priority/status and an inline checklist[]. The schema declares NO comms linkedTypes and has NO child schemas pointing at it, so it stays deliberately lean: the Data widget carries the who/when/status and the checklist, and lifecycleActions drive the status machine (available → active → completed / terminated). No files/notes/contacts/calendar leaves — a task carries none of that content; those live on the parent case. Audit history (status transitions) is a sidebar tab.

widgets.title: Case
widgets._note: task-on-the-case REQ-TASK-015: names the case this task is on, by its title, and links to it. Resolved via page slots (widget-task-case-link -> TaskCaseLink). It renders for EVERY task with a case, which is what separates it from task-waiting-case below: that one renders only for a task holding a flow run, and saying a case is waiting on an ordinary to-do would not be true. A task without a case renders nothing, and showTitle stays false so there is no empty titled box either. Not a data widget over the case field: case is a $ref and the platform renders a $ref as its uuid, which reads as broken data rather than as a way back.

widgets.title: Waiting case
widgets._note: The task half of the flow waiting relationship (case-flow-human-steps 6.1). Resolved via page slots (widget-task-waiting-case -> TaskWaitingCaseSection); names the case whose suspended run this task blocks and links to it. Renders NOTHING for a task without a flowRun, so pre-existing tasks are unchanged. showTitle stays false: an empty titled box on every ordinary task would be exactly the clutter the null render avoids.

pages.title: Case map
pages._note: Full-screen split view: a filter sidebar (case type + status) beside a CnMapWidget rendering RBAC-scoped case markers with clustering and auto-fit. Markers and overview are sourced from OpenRegister's maps-overview leaf (ADR-022, OR #154). No standard page type offers the sidebar-plus-map layout or the maps-overview declaration/points fetch lifecycle.

config._note: ADVICE-REQUEST archetype (adviesAanvraag on a case). No comms linkedTypes and no child schemas point at it, so it stays lean: the Data widget carries the request and its clock (case, adviseur, type, onderwerp, deadline, requestedAt, receivedAt, the questions[] and the returned adviesDocument), a Related panel exposes the parent case and adviser links, and lifecycleActions drive the status (aangevraagd → ontvangen / verlopen) — deadline-vs-received being the primary at-a-glance signal. No files/notes/contacts/calendar leaves: the advice document is a plain field and comms live on the parent case. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

pages.title: Processing time
pages._note: SLA / processing-time analytics. Was nominally type:dashboard but its config was ONE 12x12 widget whose slot rendered a complete second dashboard with its own <h2> — the dashboard-in-dashboard antipattern (hydra#316). Now five widgets over one shared store (src/store/modules/doorlooptijd.js). The presentational sub-components in views/doorlooptijd/components/ are unchanged; only their host moved.

config.description: SLA adherence and processing time analysis

pages.title: Process mining
pages._note: Bottleneck analysis over the case statusRecord history. The figures come from a dedicated ProcessMiningService aggregation endpoint, not a register query, so the widgets are type:custom and read one shared store (src/store/modules/processMining.js) rather than a register/schema binding. The page owns the heading, the period presets and the case-type filter; each widget renders content only — a widget that drew its own page heading would be the dashboard-in-dashboard antipattern (hydra#316).

config.description: Bottleneck analysis from recorded case status history

pages.title: Workflow Board
pages._note: Bespoke Kanban board (one column per non-final status type, drag-to-transition) rendered by a host-app SFC; no standard page type offers the drag-between-status-columns workflow surface. Mounted directly (not wrapped in a dashboard widget) so its own header is the single page title.

config._note: CONFIG/TECHNICAL archetype (WMS/WFS map-layer definition). Admin-only, no comms, no child schemas and no status lifecycle — so deliberately lean. The single Data widget holds the full endpoint config (url, layerName, srs, opacity, queryable, format, version, isDefault, active). No object-lists (nothing is a child of a layer), no content leaves (a layer carries no files/notes/calendar), no lifecycleActions (active is a plain boolean). Audit history (config edits) is a sidebar tab.

CONFIG/TECHNICAL archetype (multi-tenant provisioning record — legacy, superseded by OR Organisation). Admin-only, no comms. The Data widget carries identity + provisioning clock (slug, displayName, legalName, kvkNumber, tier, createdAt, activatedAt, terminatedAt). contractRef, isolationMode and dataResidency were dropped: none had a reader, isolationMode was a pure function of tier and dataResidency a hardcoded constant. The Provision + Refresh-usage admin actions are preserved as page actions, and lifecycleActions drive the status (onboarding → active → suspended → terminated). No object-lists or content leaves — a legacy provisioning record carries none. Audit history (provisioning events) is a sidebar tab.

WORKFLOW-RECORD archetype (inter-organisation case handover). No comms/documents and no child schemas — a transfer is a small state machine, not a dossier. The single Data widget carries the request and its resolution (caseId, sourceOrganization, targetOrganization, reason, requestedDate, rejectionReason, completedAt), and lifecycleActions drive the status (pending → accepted / rejected). No object-lists (nothing is a child of a transfer), no content leaves. Audit history (the pending→accepted/rejected transition) is a sidebar tab.

pages.title: Public appointment
pages._note: Lib gap: anonymous/token-based public pages have no v2 typed primitive — see PublicCase _note for the same architectural reason. Collapse when nc-vue adds public-page support.

pages.title: Public status
pages._note: Citizen 'track your case' page. Resolves anonymously through OpenRegister's shares-leaf #[PublicPage] endpoint GET /apps/openregister/api/public/case-tokens/{token} (ADR-022) — RBAC-respecting, public-safe fields only. Lib gap: anonymous public pages still have no v2 typed primitive; collapse when nc-vue adds public-page support.

pages.title: Federated case transfer
pages._note: Remote-org accept/reject for a federated zaakoverdracht (federated-case-collaboration). Authenticated via the transfer-scoped OpenRegister federated-share bearer token in the URL, not a local session. Lib gap: same anonymous-public-page gap as PublicStatus/PublicAppointment.

config._note: CASE-TYPE / WORKFLOW-DEFINITION archetype (the state machine that drives cases of a caseType), ADR-062 round 2. No comms. The schema splits into two genuinely distinct groups: 'Definition' (identity + versioning — title, description, caseType, version, lifecycleStatus, isActive, isDraft, parentWorkflow) and 'State machine' (the two defining graph payloads — steps[] with stages/roles/SLAs/checklists, transitions[] with from/to/guards/actions, plus editor nodePositions). Cases driven by this workflow are reached through their caseType index rather than a direct FK (case.workflowTemplate stores a version reference, not this object's id), so no object-list is scoped here. Publish/Deprecate/Clone admin actions are preserved as page actions and lifecycleActions drive the lifecycleStatus. Audit history (version changes) is a sidebar tab.

TRANSITION-RECORD archetype (an immutable entry for one case status transition). No comms/documents and it is itself a history entry, so it stays lean. The Data widget shows the transition and its side-effects (case, fromStatus→statusType, transitionLabel, noWorkflowTemplate, the evaluatedGuards[] that were checked and the dispatchedActions[] that fired); a Related panel links the parent case. No lifecycleActions — a status record is a frozen fact, not a mutable object. No content leaves. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

ASSESSMENT-RECORD archetype (a per-case LHS intervention recommendation derived from an lhsMatrix), ADR-062 round 2. No comms/documents, no child schemas. The 13-field schema splits into two genuinely distinct groups: 'Recommendation' (the matrix inputs and outcome — case, inspection, ernst, gedrag, actorType, matrixVersion, recommendedInterventie, recommendedBy) paired with the Related panel (parent case and inspection), and 'Override & final' (the accountability-bearing deviation fields — finalIntervention, override, overrideJustification, overrideBy, overrideAuthority) full-width below. No status lifecycle field and no content leaves. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

COMMITTEE archetype (bezwaaradviescommissie / BAC), ADR-062 round 2. No comms leaves on the schema. A committee is defined by its constitution and its caseload; the schema splits into two genuinely distinct groups: 'Committee' (name, type, domain, jurisdiction, quorum, active — the constitution) and 'Roster & term' (chair, secretary, members[], termStartsOn, termEndsOn, created — who sits and until when). The lead row pairs the constitution widget with an in-grid KPI stats-block (total assignments + in-deliberation workload via bacAdviceRequest.status, replacing the deprecated header summaryAggregates). Below: the roster widget full-width, then the advice-assignment object-list (bacAdviceRequest.commissie=@objectId). No status lifecycle (active is a boolean). Audit history (composition/term changes) is a sidebar tab.

content.emptyText: No advice requests assigned to this committee yet

config._note: ADVICE-ASSIGNMENT archetype (a committee advice request on a bezwaar), ADR-062 round 2. No comms leaves and no child schemas. The 15-field schema splits into two genuinely distinct groups: 'Assignment' (who/when — bezwaar, commissie, panel, status, assignedAt, deadline) paired with the Related panel (parent bezwaar and committee), and 'Advice & outcome' (the substantive opinion, dissent and evidence — advice, recommendation, conclusion, adviceIssuedAt, dissentingOpinions[], adviceDocuments, signatureEvidence, hearingReportRef) full-width below. lifecycleActions drive the status (assigned → in-deliberation → advice-issued / niet-ontvankelijk). Document references are plain fields, not a files-leaf. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

APPEAL-CASE archetype (AWB beroep at the rechtbank), ADR-062 round 2. `beroep` is a supporting schema on a unified case (beroep.case) and declares NO comms linkedTypes, so no files/notes/contacts/calendar here — those live on the parent CaseDetail. The 17-field schema splits into two genuinely distinct groups: 'Appeal' (the court header — case, sourceBezwaar, contestedDecision, courtReference, responsibleChamber, competentCourt) paired with the Related panel (parent case and source bezwaar), and 'Filing & judgment' (the clock, sub-process and outcome — appellantFilingDate/NotifiedDate, filingDeadline, voorzieningRequested, latefilingNotice, fileInspectionRequests[], judgmentOutcome/Date/Document, cascadeAction/cascadeBezwaarCase) full-width below. No status enum on this schema, so no lifecycleActions. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

pages.title: Reports
pages._note: ADR-112: one page of cards rather than a Reports submenu. The three report pages stay routable — deep links, e2e specs and these cards all address them by route NAME — they simply leave the navigation. Their menu entries are retired in src/menu-layout.json under `removals`.

pages.title: Deadline monitoring
pages._note: Deadline-monitoring KPIs plus the quarterly report and annual dwangsom audit. The figures come from /api/termijn/* aggregation endpoints, not a register query, so the widgets are type:custom over one shared store (src/store/modules/termijnDashboard.js). The page owns the heading and the case-type filter; the quarter and year inputs stay inside their own widgets because they scope THAT report, not the page.

config.description: Deadline compliance, quarterly reporting and the annual dwangsom audit

pages.title: Substitutions & reassignment
pages._note: Coordinator substitution console: a filterable list of all substitutions plus register-on-behalf, revoke, inspect-capacity-stamped-actions, and bulk-reassignment actions (the latter two open dedicated modals). Coordinator role is enforced server-side. The standard list type cannot host the on-behalf-of register flow, the action-list inspection, or the bulk-reassign operation over the listed objects.

pages.title: Case types

config._folderSidebarNote: `source: "field"` and not `source: "facet"`: CnIndexPage resolves exactly four sources -- register, field, custom and files -- and an unknown one falls through to `custom`, whose folder list is the (absent) `folders` array, so a sidebar declared as a facet renders an empty pane. `field` derives the folders from the distinct `category` values of the rows themselves, which is what a free-word category can offer. `facetable: true` on the property is what makes the value filterable at all; `x-openregister-facet` is read by nothing.

pages._note: A case type is the blueprint every case is governed by — lifecycle, deadlines, classification, the workflow that drives it — and `case.caseType` references it. It had no surface at all: the original `CaseTypesMenu` pointed at the in-app `/settings` page, which page-topology-cleanup B1 retired for mounting AdminRoot through the in-app router (ADR-004), and no replacement was ever built. The capability went with the page and only its stale `settingsSection` id was left behind. WorkflowDefinitionDetail's own note still says cases are 'reached through their caseType index', naming this page. Restored as an ordinary schema-driven index rather than by reviving the retired settings route.

pages.title: Case type

widgets.title: Personal data
widgets._note: The AVG facts belong to the case TYPE, not to a case: whether this process touches personal data, which categories, on what article 6 basis, and which activity in OpenRegister's verwerkingsregister the cases are logged under. `hideEmpty` stays off, because an unanswered basis is exactly what a data protection officer is looking for -- an empty row is the finding.

widgets.title: Versions
widgets._note: The type's workflowTemplate rows: what was published, when, and what the change note said. A DECLARED object-list and not the blueprint widget, because a workflowTemplate belongs to exactly one case type -- there is no inheritance to merge here, so `caseType = @objectId` is the whole question. `description` is the column the change note is written into by the publish action.

columns.label: Updated
columns._note: `updated` is NOT a workflowTemplate property: the timestamp lives on OpenRegister's metadata envelope, and a column bound to a property the schema does not declare renders a dash in every row without saying so. `WorkflowDefinitions` spells it the same way. Caught by ManifestColumnBindingTest, which is exactly what that test exists for.

content.emptyText: This case type has no published versions yet

widgets.title: Statuses, results and attributes
widgets._note: The one widget on this page that a declared type cannot be. An object-list fetches OpenRegister itself, so the only question it can ask is `statusType where caseType = @objectId` -- the type's OWN rows. A type that derives its lifecycle from a parent has none of those, so three declared lists would render three empty tables about a case type that plainly has four statuses, and nothing would say so. The merge exists only in CaseTypeResolver, and /api/case-types/{id}/blueprint is how a page reads it. It sits in the LAYOUT and not inside a tab strip on purpose: a `type: "custom"` widget named as a tab CHILD resolves by registry TYPE, finds nothing, and renders an empty panel without logging anything.

config._headerActionsNote: There is no `run-action` header-action type. The manifest schema enumerates handler, open-modal, open-page, navigate, object-op, export, open-form, refresh, api-call, agent and toggle, and CnActionButtons resolves exactly those; the design's `run-action` would have been refused by `npm run check:manifest` and, had it slipped through, rendered a button that dispatches nothing. Export is an `api-call` with `download: true`, which is the shape that asks for the response as a blob and hands it to the browser -- the endpoint already answers a DataDownloadResponse. The other three are dialogs, each for a reason a declarative action cannot meet: Import takes a FILE (a confirm gate has no fields and an api-call sends JSON), Publish must show the validation findings BEFORE asking for a change note, and Duplicate must land on the copy rather than refresh the page you are already on. Every icon here is registered in src/icons.js (gate-60); a name that is not renders no icon at all. The three dialogs read the case type off the ROUTE and not off their props: `open-modal` forwards props verbatim, so a `@objectId` token would arrive as that literal string.

headerActions.label: Export
headerActions.errorMessage: The case type could not be exported.

pages._note: The case-type blueprint: identity and classification, the processing deadline and extension rules (AWB terms), the pinned workflowDefinition, sub-case types and decision types. Cases of this type are reached from the Cases index filtered by caseType rather than duplicated here. `case-type-authoring-extras` put the type's own content on the page: what it inherits from a parent, what it actually offers, the personal data it processes, and the four gestures that were API-only. NO TAB STRIP: `case-type-one-authoring-surface` owns that, and building one here would be the second strip the moment it lands. These are layout cells, and they become that strip's children when it arrives -- except `case-type-blueprint`, which cannot be a tab child while it is `type: "custom"`.

pages.title: Store
pages._note: ADR-080: the store plane. Discovery belongs to OpenRegister — this page reads /api/store/items, which is a thin action over AppHost's GenericStoreService, so the SSRF guard, the redirect refusal and the token live in the engine and dossiq builds no registry URL. A custom component rather than type:index because store items are REMOTE objects: the object-backed index renderer resolves a local register+schema and cannot address them. With no registry configured the engine answers not_configured WITHOUT a network call and the page renders dossiq's built-in templates, which is Decision 4 and the only reason this surface may carry the word Store at all. Install is dossiq's own and admin-guarded (Decision 3), and it writes case CONFIGURATION only — the record schemas are refused. PLACEMENT: footer, order 92, between Documentation (90) and Reports (95). openbuild, hermiq and integriq put Store in the main section instead; ADR-080 records no placement decision, so one of the two conventions is wrong and the ADR needs an amendment either way.

pages.title: Flows
pages._note: ADR-110 Decision 4: a flow is app-specific — a dossiq flow operates on cases — so the authoring surface lives here rather than behind a deep link to OpenRegister's list. An ordinary index over the NAMED flows source: a flow lives in the shared native flow store, not a register/schema, so the object-backed index cannot address it. Scoped app="dossiq" — the same store OpenRegister, integriq and hermiq use, so list/status semantics stay identical fleet-wide. rowRoute names the FlowDetail page (a route NAME, not a path): a named-source page has no register+schema, so CnPageRenderer cannot infer a detail page, and without an explicit target the row click and the Edit action fall back to the source's /flows path rather than the page this manifest declares. Mirrors openregister/src/manifest.json:flows.

pages.title: Flow
pages._note: The shared CnFlowDetail node/edge canvas over the same native flow store OpenRegister and hermiq use — not an app-owned editor. Controls live in the NcAppSidebar (sidebarComponent) so the canvas gets full width; canvas and sidebar share useFlowStore. Mirrors openregister/src/manifest.json:flowDetail.

observability._note: Declarative observability via OpenRegister's AppHost engine (ADR-040). Reproduces the output of the now-deleted hand-written HealthController + MetricsController. The /api/health and /api/metrics routes are aliased to AppHost\Controller\GenericHealth#index / GenericMetrics#index, so the engine reads this block at request time. Parity: metric names (with the engine-added dossiq_ prefix), types, HELP texts and label keys (incl. the caseType JSON field surfacing as the case_type label) match the pre-adoption contract; the implicit dossiq_info / dossiq_up gauges are emitted by the engine. The APCu controller-local cache is replaced by the engine's per-metric cacheTtl via the distributed cache (same 30s/60s TTLs, shared across workers).
